item.title: Ex-UFC fighter MVP signs with KSI's Misfits Boxing
item.description: Former UFC fighter Michael 'Venom' Page says he is "coming to show the boxing world what I can do".
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Former UFC fighter Michael 'Venom' Page says he is "coming to show the boxing world what I can do" after joining the Misfits promotion outfit.

The 39-year-old's last fight on his UFC contract took place in September when he beat Nursulton Ruziboev to register a fifth win in six fights since making his debut for the organisation in 2024.

Despite his record in the UFC, Page, known as MVP, was dropped by the MMA promotion and is linking up with Misfits Boxing.

The Londoner has signed a "multi-fight, multi-year agreement".

"I've been in combat sports for a long time and I've had plenty of options, but MF Sports is the right fit for me," said Page.

"They're doing things differently, the energy is huge, and the fights are big.

"I'm excited for this new chapter, and I'm coming to show the boxing world what I can do. I feel free, shackles are off."

Page has won 26 of his 29 MMA fights and is a decorated kickboxer.

The former Bellator star made his professional boxing debut in 2017 and is 2-0, but has not boxed since 2018.

KSI, a co-founder of Misfits, announced MVP's arrival at an event on Saturday.

"Michael Venom Page is one of the biggest names in combat sports, and everyone wanted him," said the influencer, musician and former boxer.

"For him to choose Misfits says everything about where we are as a promotion. He's a superstar, he's explosive, and fans are going to love watching him in the ring with us."

item.title: Ulster playing games like they're training sessions - Murphy
item.description: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like they're training sessions" as he expressed his disappointment with his side's slow start in Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.

Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.

Having opened the campaign with a home defeat by Edinburgh and a 33-33 draw in Glasgow, Murphy's side remain winless on the domestic front before starting their European campaign next week.

"We're still very much in the early part of the season. We've got three our four players coming back in for their first games this weekend," said Murphy.

"The flow of the team hasn't completely settled in. At the moment, we're playing matches like they're training sessions.

"We're overplaying with the ball in the middle of the park, we need to start applying more pressure to the opposition.

"That's going to be a key part that we need to learn from this week."

'We allowed Munster to set the tempo'

Despite the return of Ireland internationals Stockdale, McCloskey and Nick Timoney, Ulster struggled against a powerful display from Munster in the first half as tries from Alex Kendellen (2), Marnus van der Merwe and Dan Kelly put Clayton McMillan's side in the driving seat at the break.

But despite a spirited second-half showing to earn another three points after last week's draw in Glasgow, Murphy said he was "bitterly disappointed" when asked if he was left with mixed emotions.

"We allowed Munster to set the tempo, we were inaccurate with our first launch, so that we kicked off, they kicked out, so we were inaccurate with that first launch," added Murphy.

"Off the back of that, penalty, penalty and then you're back in your corner and fighting for your life.

"Once you're five metres out and the opposition have a line-out, it's very hard to stop, so that gave them control of the first half."

Having pegged Munster back, Ulster could have won the game with the final play, but Robert Baloucoune's attempted pass to Matthew Devine was cut out by Alex Nankivell as the hosts' winless URC run stretched to seven games.

"Coming in at half-time, I thought the lads reacted really well," added Murphy.

"We made some changes, still very inaccurate in the second half and didn't look after the ball well enough, didn't control field position at all in the game, but ultimately we got into a situation where last play of the game we were running at them and gave them the ball back again.

"Our turnover rate needs to come down, our scrum has been going really well but took a backward step tonight and I kind of feel like we didn't attack the game the way we needed to."

Munster boss McMillan was similarly downbeat after his side were held scoreless in the second half to let slip a 21-point advantage.

"We talked about it at half-time that Ulster are a quality side that won't go away," he said.

"We needed to continue to be accurate and just apply pressure in the right parts of the field.

"But we didn't quite get the same quality of possession in the second half, and Ulster were good enough to find a way back into the game."

item.title: 'I kissed Rodrigo and said thanks' - De Zerbi 'liked' Spurs red card
item.description: Roberto de Zerbi praises Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in a 1-1 draw against Manchester United.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi praised Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in the 1-1 draw against Manchester United.

The Uruguay midfielder was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a feisty 78th-minute melee when Spurs were trailing 1-0 at Old Trafford.

Despite being reduced to 10 men, Tottenham managed to salvage a point as Dominic Solanke headed home in the second minute of added time.

Spurs remain winless in the Premier League this season after six games, but De Zerbi was thankful to Bentancur for providing a "spark" against United.

"I kiss Rodrigo and say thanks," De Zerbi said in his post-match press conference.

"In that moment maybe with 10 players we played with more courage, more energy.

"For a long time Tottenham played without this blood, this character."

The incident happened when Shaw, on the receiving end of a reckless challenge by Bentancur, raced towards the Spurs player and shoved him off the pitch.

Bentancur reacted by planting his head towards Shaw's face. The pair were separated by their team-mates before referee Stuart Attwell sent the substitute off.

De Zerbi said it was a "mistake" by Bentancur, but added it was the type of reaction Tottenham needed to finish the game.

"I kissed Bentancur in the dressing room because we need this type of reaction, this character. Football is character," he told Sky Sports.

"I liked the situation with the red card. We need at this moment the situation, not to bring a red card but we need to not accept the defeat."

'First time we played like a team' - could this be a turning point for Spurs?

Despite the late elation sparked by Solanke's 92nd-minute equaliser, Tottenham remain in the relegation zone with just three points from their opening six matches.

It is just the fourth time the club have failed to win each of their opening six games of a league season, after 2008-09, 1955-56 and 1912-13.

Spurs have often looked lively in attack this season, but they have lacked conviction in front of goal and only 19th-placed Coventry have scored fewer goals than Tottenham's three.

However, Tottenham fans can take belief from their overall performance at Old Trafford as they ran United ragged in the opening half with fluid, high-tempo football.

"Today has been the game where for the first time this season we showed we are a team," De Zerbi said.

"We played for the team-mates, we played together, we stayed inside of the game in every situation and we attacked as a team and defended as a team."

The Italian manager added on Sky Sports: "I'm very happy because I've seen the right spirit, the right character and I want to start from this character, this reaction, this behaviour."

Tottenham spent more than £250m on new talent over the summer - adding 10 players to their squad.

But their poor start has prompted the club to organise a warm-weather training camp in Spain, with the team expected to travel to Marbella on Sunday in the hope it will provide a chance for their new-look squad to bond.

"Now the target is to build the team," De Zerbi said.

"We are a great group of players but we are not a team yet and to be a team is to play for the team-mates, suffer together, attack together."

Spurs face newly-promoted Coventry on Monday, 19 October before making the short trip to Chelsea the following Saturday.

item.title: Boos, anguish & fading belief -'worrying day' for under-pressure Carrick
item.description: It couldn't happen again could it? Another failure to beat 10 men increases pressure on Man Utd boss Michael Carrick after a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

For the second time in successive home Premier League games, Manchester United failed to beat opponents reduced to 10 men.

For the third time in as many seasons, a United manager finds himself under severe pressure before the clocks have gone back.

Four weeks ago, Manchester City needed an incorrect video assistant referee (VAR) decision to take advantage of an ineffective United performance after Phil Foden had been shown a red card in the 23rd minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

On Saturday, the damage was self-inflicted as a Spurs side, who had given every indication of being unable to score before Rodrigo Bentancur's headfirst charge at Luke Shaw just five minutes after Bryan Mbeumo's opener, came up with an injury-time equaliser.

Centre-back Lisandro Martinez was outmuscled embarrassingly easily by Dominic Solanke, with goalkeeper Senne Lammens failing to read the striker's deft touch that crept in at the far corner.

The anguish on United faces told its own story.

"A worrying day for Michael Carrick," observed former United skipper Gary Neville on Sky Sports.

First, a couple of sorry statistics.

  • Manchester United have just six points from their opening six games of the Premier League season, their fewest at this stage of a league campaign since 1986-87, when they amassed four under Sir Alex Ferguson.

  • They have failed to win five of their six Premier League games this season (D3 L2), already as many as in 17 league games under Michael Carrick last season (W12 D3 L2).

  • United have collected two points from their last two games, both of which were against teams who began the match at the bottom of the Premier League.

  • In points terms they are closer to the relegation zone than the Champions League spots.

Carrick's side are now winless in four league games and face an always tricky trip across the Pennines to face old rivals Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday, 18 October. Either side of that are daunting Champions League trips to Atletico Madrid and Como.

United officials have repeatedly offered their backing to Carrick in recent weeks.

However, no fan needs reminding that two seasons ago a run of two wins in nine games in all competitions put Erik ten Hag under severe pressure before the axe fell after a defeat at West Ham on 27 October.

Last season, a combination of a shocking EFL Cup exit at the hands of League Two Grimsby and an insipid 3-1 loss at Brentford on 27 September did so much to undermine confidence in Ruben Amorim before he was sacked on 5 January.

The start to this campaign is starting to look increasingly familiar.

'I don't feel let down'

"I'm not happy with he amount of points we've got so far, for sure, you know," said Carrick.

"I'm not hiding, there's no hiding from that. I think it could have been different for a couple of little things here or there, but the reality is the reality, we've got to accept it, you know. We need to put things in a direction, in a positive direction quite quickly, that's pretty plain."

The 'little things' Carrick talks about are the defending for Solanke's goal, the lack of pressure put on Everton's Ainsley Maitland-Niles when he smashed another injury-time equaliser at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on 6 September, and the preventable Martinez own goal that nearly gave Fulham victory at Craven Cottage just before the international break.

"We've got to be a little bit more streetwise in moments, a little bit more stubborn and a little bit stronger in seeing out certain things," he added.

"It doesn't change my belief or the confidence in the players, you know. We're a really good team and capable of being a really good team, but we've obviously got to start getting more points on the board, that's for sure."

The problem is with each disappointment, the belief of United being 'a really good team' starts to ebb away.

Yet again, a post-match focus centred on how much Carrick's team ran, even though running for the sake of it has proved to be of little benefit.

"The stats don't lie when every time the other team runs more than you," said Sky Sports pundit and former Spurs captain Jamie Redknapp.

"Tottenham ran 5km more than Man United. OK, they had 10 men but that is every game. If you outrun your opposing number, you will win games. I'm not saying they are not trying. It is that physical battle they are losing though."

It feels as though some fans are losing faith already, judging by the way they reacted at moments during the game, aside from the boos that accompanied the end of each half.

Forward Matheus Cunha - one of a number of Carrick's squad who have failed to reproduce the form he showed in the second half of last season - gestured to the crowd during the opening period. It wasn't clear whether he was responding to a negative comment or urging more noise, but the Brazilian clearly wasn't happy.

Carrick's family are season ticket holders. He knows what it is like to watch United struggle at Old Trafford.

"Obviously, it hurts," he said. "It hurts a lot. It's not nice to go through. I care as much as anybody about this place. Sometimes you could say too much because then it overspills. But it's coming from a good place, really, and so I understand it."

It is in moments like this that Carrick, who presents such a calm front in public, must be churning inside.

He knows how the pressure can mount around Old Trafford and how fierce the debate around the club in the search for answers can be.

As he said, Carrick cares. And he is certain his players feel the same.

"I don't feel let down," he added. "You can make mistakes.

"We've all got standards; we've all got levels. The players hold their hands up at times when something goes against them.

"It's not like everyone walks off into the distance tonight like everything's fine and it's left on me. It's not that at all. The players care, for sure.

"I don't feel let down by them for making a mistake. We've just got to all help each other be better, and it's on me to help them and guide them through it."

item.title: Leinster stroll past Cardiff for happy homecoming
item.description: Champions Leinster score five tries to beat Cardiff in Dublin for their first win of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship campaign.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

United Rugby Championship

Leinster (22) 29

Tries: Keenan, J O'Brien 2, Conan, Osborne Cons: Prendergast 2

Cardiff (5) 5

Tries: Grady

Champions Leinster made a successful return to the revamped Laya Arena by beating Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

The Irish province recorded their first victory of the 2026-27 season in front of 20,600 supporters, and condemned the Blue and Blacks to a first loss.

Leinster scored three tries inside the first quarter through Hugo Keenan, Jimmy O'Brien and Jack Conan, then O'Brien's second in the 37th minute secured the four-try bonus.

But, with a raft of Ireland internationals making their first outings of the campaign, the second half was flat and scoreless until Jamie Osborne went over with five minutes to go.

Cardiff failed to claim a URC match point just once when making the play-offs last season, but left Dublin without anything after being limited to Mason Grady's first-half try.

Leo Cullen's side started the defence of their title in South Africa and returned with three bonus points from defeats by Lions and Sharks.

The head coach brought back his big hitters to ensure it was a successful return to the redeveloped €52m Laya Arena, formerly the RDS Arena, after two seasons playing at Aviva Stadium.

A sell-out crowd was treated to a glitzy pre-match show and then a rapid Leinster start, with the hosts hitting the front when full-back Keenan kicked ahead and gathered after being found on the left wing by fast handling.

Cardiff scrum-half Aled Davies was sin-binned for cynically killing the ball on his line and tries followed by wing O'Brien and number eight Conan.

It looked set to be a long night for the Welsh side but they made light of being a man down to make it 15-5 thanks to the cunning of Callum Sheedy.

The Wales fly-half caught Leinster sleeping from a penalty to find Grady on the wing with a cross-kick.

But the hosts were in control at half-time thanks to a set play that foxed Cardiff to give O'Brien a run-in for a fourth try down the same flank, Sam Prendergast kicking his first conversion for a 22-5 lead.

Cardiff lacked the power - or accuracy - to make a dent in the Leinster defence from several entries into the 22 after the restart.

The Welsh side had plenty of territory and showed tenacity in a subdued atmosphere, but it was centre Osborne that got the first score of the half in the closing stages with a strong finish from close range.

Faletau comeback delayed

Cardiff named eight Taulupe Faletau in their starting line-up on Thursday afternoon, although boss Corniel van Zyl admitted the Wales number eight still had a few boxes to tick because of niggles.

The Blue and Blacks opted against fielding the 35-year-old for the first time since a shoulder injury suffered at Sharks in March.

In-form Taine Basham was a late inclusion and continued his strong start to the season as his side's most dynamic carrier.

Cardiff travel to free-flowing Northampton in the Champions Cup on Sunday, 18 October (17:30 BST).

With a five-day turnaround from that fixture to a home URC game against Sharks, they must choose the right time to reintegrate Faletau.

Leinster: Keenan; Kenny, Ringrose, Osborne, J O'Brien; Prendergast, Coffey, Usanov, Sheehan (capt), Furlong, McCarthy, Ryan, Deegan, Penny, Conan.

Replacements: Kelleher, Dooley, Clarkson, Spicer, Ericson, Gunne, Gabriel, Henshaw.

Cardiff: Young; Beetham, Millard, Malan, Grady; Sheedy, Davies; Southworth, Belcher (capt), Sebastian, McNally, T Williams, Mann, Thomas, Faletau.

Replacements: E Lloyd, Barratt, Wainwright, Nott, Paea, Mulder, J Evans, S Emanuel.

Yellow: Aled Davies 16.

Referee: Sam Grove-White (Scotland)

Assistant referees: Keane Davison (Ireland), Jonathan Erskine (Ireland)

TMO: Andrew McMenemy (Scotland)

item.title: 'Reminds me of Muller' - Naderi proving worth in Rangers revival
item.description: After a slow start to his Rangers career, striker Ryan Naderi is playing an integral role in the club's title challenge and proving his doubters wrong.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

A previously unfancied striker is playing a crucial role in Rangers' revival - and even earning comparisons with Germany legend Thomas Muller.

Ryan Naderi pounced for a first-half double against Kilmarnock as Derek McInnes' side overcame the disruption of the extended international break to earn a sixth straight league win and rise to the top of the Scottish Premiership.

That outcome enhanced a turnaround in fortunes for Rangers after the disappointment of their European exit, having also taken just a point from their first two Premiership games.

They now lie a point ahead of Celtic, who visit Motherwell on Sunday under pressure to regain their place at the top.

Much of the focus has centred on an excellent defensive record with just one league goal conceded in their previous five Premiership games - that record blemished by Nicky Clesenco's late Kilmarnock consolation.

However, at the top end of the pitch, Naderi is defying those who doubted his ability to make a consistent impact.

Former Rangers forward Peter Lovenkrands has been impressed by what he's seen from the German-born Czech Republic striker.

"Naderi at times does things where you're like 'How did he do that?'" Lovenkrands said on BBC Sportsound.

"He reminds me a lot of Thomas Muller - he's not nice on the eye at times, but he creates stuff because he's so unorthodox."

Naderi steps up in absence of Shankland and Chermiti

Naderi now has three goals in his past two league games, having scored the winner in Rangers' 1-0 league win away to Celtic before the break.

That alone elevated his status among an initially sceptical support who had watched the 23-year-old struggle to make an impact after signing from German third-tier side Hansa Rostock in February.

Just one league goal - and two in a League Cup trouncing of Queen's Park - followed last season, with observers unconvinced he had the attributes to be a starting striker at the club.

Such assessments seem to have dissipated as he has surged to the fore in the absence of injured team-mates Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti.

Six goals and three assists, often key interventions, have elevated his status as he adds end product to his physical prowess.

A crucial assist in the late win over St Mirren when Bojan Miovski scored a vital winner was notable.

Naderi has netted winners against Motherwell and Celtic and his two goals against Kilmarnock proved decisive.

His manager agrees Naderi, who made his Czech Republic debut last week, has stepped up to the plate for Rangers at a good time.

"Yes, and fair play to him," McInnes said. "He's always such an honest boy, he's willing to put defenders under pressure.

"I've always felt as a striker that if the ball goes in the box, he'll score his goals. He's not the type of striker that creates a lot for himself, so he needs that service.

"If we put the ball in the box, as we did in the first half, then he looks a threat.

"He's had such a good few weeks. Everybody's so pleased for him. We need someone who would regularly be the goalscorer here at the club."

Rangers now look a 'McInnes side'

McInnes cited fatigue and the extended break as reasons for his side not kicking on from leading 3-0 by half-time against Kilmarnock.

The visitors were unfortunate to only pull one goal back as Rangers toiled in the second half.

That said, it's now seven wins in a row in all competitions, with strikers firing backed up by a defensive solidity that might have fans believing this could be their season for a first league title since 2021.

Former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday has more faith now in McInnes' side, telling BBC Sportsound: "A lot of my confidence doesn't come from Rangers being brilliant, it comes from Celtic being poor.

"Rangers are definitely building. They are becoming a much more predictable side - you go into games fancying them to win.

"You're starting to see a Derek McInnes side - really solid defensively and creating chances."

McInnes admitted Rangers' second-half performance was "far from where we needed to be", but wants the club to "feel good about ourselves" after topping the table for the first time this season.

"There's a bit of understanding for me where the players have been. This break's been far too long," he said.

"But we've got the job done, and credit the players for digging deep and getting three points."

item.title: Savage success and statement win for Boro - Sam Parkin's EFL Takeaways
item.description: BBC Final Score pundit Sam Parkin looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including Robbie Savage's debut as Peterborough manager.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

After the three-week international break, there was a full programme once again across the EFL on a day full of talking points. Final Score pundit and former Swindon, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker Sam Parkin selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

Savage's front foot style should suit Posh

Robbie Savage enjoyed a dream afternoon on his debut as an EFL manager as his Peterborough United side inflicted more misery on Leicester City and Russell Martin with a 3-1 victory at King Power Stadium.

Parkin: "What a start for Robbie Savage, going back to the club where he's probably most synonymous. There's been a lot talked and written about him this week when we don't have too great a knowledge of what he's like as a manager considering his journey so far through non-league.

"I'm very open-minded about the appointment and what he can do. I've heard he wants to play with real intensity and really play aggressively from the front.

"I thought this could be a good game for him against a Leicester City team that have a unique style of play but take risks with the ball, so in terms of a game plan, it's probably worked perfectly the way he wants his team to play.

"It's only a start but he's inherited a brilliant scorer in Harry Leonard, so he doesn't have to worry about who will convert chances. It's a young team, it probably needs a bit of experience in the window ahead but I think they've got better players than their current position shows, so it's a great opportunity for Robbie.

"Dealing with the heavier scrutiny from where he's been previously will be a challenge and naturally he'll have a target on his back because of who he is and that personality.

"Peterborough have always been a really attacking and free-scoring team in the last 10 to 15 years, that's what I associate with them, and it sounds like that's the way he wants to go about things so that should be met with open arms."

Lankshear's goals missing link for Boro

Middlesbrough celebrated their '150 Fixture' with a narrow win over Wolves, which took them into the Championship's top two. After the week in which Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert discovered his punishment for his part in the Spygate affair, Boro are going the right way to put those emotional events of May behind them.

Parkin: "You look at the way Coventry were promoted last season after their brilliant finish to the previous one and I see a lot of similarities with Middlesbrough - the timescales that the bosses were in charge being one of them.

"Boro came very close last season and the one gaping hole in their squad was an out-and-out goalscorer. They created so many chances, they were brilliant between both boxes, a great watch but they couldn't convert those chances.

"So to bring in Will Lankshear and for him to have had the start he's had could be pivotal in their push for promotion.

"Today Kim Hellberg got his best back four on the pitch, so I felt that was a real stand-out moment in the season, to keep a clean sheet against a good Wolves team because they have been conceding too many goals. So I expect them to really kick on from here."

Change in style at right time for Davies

Birmingham City came out on top in the lunchtime derby, grabbing a one-goal win away to West Bromwich Albion. It was a third win on the road already this season and lifted them into the expanded play-off spots in seventh, as ambitious Blues aim to get in the promotion mix after a slightly disappointing 10th place last season.

Parkin: "In League One, they got promoted playing really stylish football, trying to play out from the back at all costs.

"They can still do that but they're definitely a more direct team this season, there's a better balance and they are more forceful from set-pieces.

"The change has come at just about the perfect time for Chris Davies because he was under enormous pressure. They had to start winning because you know how ambitious they are as a club, how big the support is and how demanding they are.

"Davies rolled the dice and at the moment it's paid off in a big way. Now they just need to start winning at St Andrew's - four draws so far - and if they do that, they can be a force to be reckoned with in the Championship."

Hard winter ahead for Alexander and North End

Graham Alexander has swapped a possible League One promotion push with Bradford City for the lower end of the Championship with Preston North End, and his homecoming to Deepdale had an inauspicious start as defeat by Millwall sent them bottom.

Parkin: "I don't think it's going to be a huge improvement overnight at Preston, but you can understand the appointment as he's a club legend, which is nice.

"Graham Alexander really knows how to set a team up. His strength has always been in the organisation, rather than being a manager of free-flowing attack-minded sides.

"I have no doubt his side will start keeping clean sheets, it's whether they've got the attacking players in the building or whether he can free them up to start scoring more. That would be my question mark.

"He deserves the opportunity, the work he did at Bradford was incredible but I don't feel it's a brilliant Preston squad that he's inherited.

"Given the way they've started, survival would be deemed a success this season, then consolidating with the aid of a few transfer windows and trying to improve the squad."

Too early to call Salford promotion certainties

Salford City are top of League Two after a sixth win in seven matches, courtesy of a 2-0 success at Cheltenham Town. But are the Ammies the team to beat in League Two this season?

Parkin: "Karl Robinson fell at the final hurdle last season and I felt it was quite a harsh sacking as he's probably the one manager who looked like he was going to achieve the target of promotion.

"Peter Cklamovski has inherited a good squad and they've certainly got the players to go one better than last year. To add to that, they've got Macaulay Langstaff who scored freely for Notts County and Luke Molyneux, a stand-out performer for Doncaster.

"But it's still early days. Barnet are very free-scoring and to remain unbeaten is credit to them at this stage of the season. Crewe are another team that won today and have had a taste of the play-offs and had a terrific start to the season.

"I would also throw York and Bristol Rovers into the mix so I'll withhold judgement on Salford until I see a little bit more football."

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's Adam Lanigan.

item.title: Arbeloa 'doesn't feel fear' but pressure increases after loss
item.description: Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa says he does not 'feel fear' after defeat at Ipswich left his side winless in six games and bottom of the Premier League.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Six games, no wins and bottom of the table - it is fair to say it has been a difficult start to life as a Premier League manager for Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

The Cottagers were on the cusp of victory at Ipswich on Saturday but the hosts scored twice after the 88th minute to snatch a 2-1 win.

It is the second successive game in the league that Fulham have led approaching the final few minutes, only to concede.

It means they have just two points to show so far, increasing the pressure on Arbeloa to improve his side's fortunes.

"I never worry about my position," said former Real Madrid manager Arbeloa.

"I don't feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it. You have to work, take the decision and you need to show confidence to your players.

"For me I am so happy with many things that they are doing. I know it is not easy for them.

"It's not about my position, it is about Fulham's position. That is the most important thing. Obviously it is just six games, but it is true we need points."

Late goals proving costly

When Marco Silva was appointed Fulham boss in 2021 he brought a stability to the club that ensured they were competitive in the Premier League, without ever really being in danger of being relegated.

Silva departed in the summer to become head coach of Benfica and in appointing Arbeloa as his replacement, Fulham were undoubtedly taking a bit of a gamble.

The former Liverpool and Real Madrid player arrived with limited managerial experience at senior level, having had a brief spell in charge of Real Madrid from January until May this year.

The biggest problem Fulham have had under him is conceding late goals, with his side having let in goals in the final 15 minutes in four of their six Premier League matches.

Despite that, Arbeola was defiant after the Ipswich defeat, insisting he is right man for the job at Fulham, and he can handle the pressure of needing to turn things around.

"Maybe you don't know me but I played for the best team in world. I have coached the best team in the world," he said.

"Maybe you don't know, but just to let you know, that pressure is part of my life since I was a kid.

"So, it is normal in football. It is normal for players, it is normal for coaches and everybody that is around a team.

"I think pressure is something that is important for me and I like it."

Crucial period coming up

The Ipswich match marked the first of three games in a row where Fulham face a newly promoted side.

They host Hull on Saturday, 17 October before travelling to Coventry a week later and failure to win at least one of those fixtures would increase the pressure further on Arbeloa.

"We need to take a hard look at ourselves," said Ryan Sessegnon, who had put Fulham ahead at Ipswich.

"It's a bit of mentality thing at the moment. We need to try and demand more from ourselves.

"We need to set higher standards for ourselves because it's going to be a hard season."
